Score REO-pairratio within-sample log-ratio discriminator

Source: R/singlesample-reo-scorers.R
score_reo_pairratio.Rd

Scores each specimen with the pairwise log-ratio coefficients learned by fit_reo_pairratio. Each available pair (a, b) contributes its frozen coefficient times log(X[i, a] + pseudocount) - log(X[i, b] + pseudocount). With the default strict = FALSE, pairs missing either feature are omitted. The frozen intercept and remaining coefficients are unchanged; there is no rescaling. This is a reduced-support linear predictor, not the complete fitted model's score. Its discrimination and calibration on a reduced panel are not established by the complete-panel fit. The returned score is the linear predictor, not plogis() of it.

Empty or constant fitted support, absence of all required features, all-nondetect rows, and panels without a complete pair raise a singlesample_input_error; see score_specimen. Scoring uses no random numbers and no scored-batch statistics.

Usage

score_reo_pairratio(model, X, meta = NULL, strict = FALSE)

Arguments

model

A reo_pairratio_model object returned by fit_reo_pairratio.

X

Numeric matrix (samples \(\times\) features) of non-negative abundance values. Columns must be named feature ids.

meta

Optional per-sample metadata. Accepted for interface uniformity and ignored by this method.

strict

Logical scalar. The default FALSE preserves scoring over available pairs for backward compatibility. Set TRUE to reject any missing feature from a fitted pair. Unused training features are not required. Existing invalid-input and unusable-support checks apply in both modes.

Value

Numeric vector of one finite linear-predictor score per row. Larger scores are more case-like. The support attribute is a data frame with one row per score: n_available counts fitted pairs with both named columns present, n_fitted counts all fitted pairs, and full_support reports whether these counts agree. Counts describe column availability, not detection or assay quality. Save attr(score, "support") before subsetting or numeric coercion, which can discard attributes.

References

Aitchison J. (1986) The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data. Chapman and Hall.

Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R. (2010) Regularization paths for generalized linear models via coordinate descent. Journal of Statistical Software 33: 1-22.

Examples

# An illustrative frozen two-pair model.
pairs <- data.frame(feature_a = c("a", "c"), feature_b = c("b", "d"))
model <- structure(list(selected_pairs = pairs, coefficients = c(2, -1),
                        intercept = 0.25, pseudocount = 0.5),
                   class = "reo_pairratio_model")
X <- rbind(c(a = 2, b = 1, c = 1, d = 3), c(a = 1, b = 2, c = 4, d = 2))
full <- score_reo_pairratio(model, X, strict = TRUE)
partial <- score_reo_pairratio(model, X[, c("a", "b"), drop = FALSE])
attr(partial, "support")  # 1 available / 2 fitted pairs; full_support = FALSE
#>   n_available n_fitted full_support
#> 1           1        2        FALSE
#> 2           1        2        FALSE
expected <- 0.25 + 2 * (log(X[, "a"] + 0.5) - log(X[, "b"] + 0.5))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(partial), expected)))
tryCatch(score_reo_pairratio(model, X[, c("a", "b"), drop = FALSE], strict = TRUE),
         singlesample_input_error = function(e) e$code)
#> [1] "MISSING_REQUIRED_FEATURES"
